li.label: copied the old writing
li.description: Three days in the vault in the hill, copying out the walls by lamplight. I keep thinking about the people who wrote it all down and never came back to read it.

li.label: the sleeper stayed
li.description: The sleeper from the hill woke up and decided to stay with us. I was the one sitting by the bed.

li.label: a debt repaid
li.description: The stranger we hid that night came back to pay what was owed, and more. I told the others they would.

li.label: gave up an innocent
li.description: We pointed the riders up the road. The stranger they were chasing had done nothing wrong, and we helped them anyway.

li.label: a wedding at our place
li.description: Two families who couldn't stand each other got married under our roof. I danced until my feet hurt.

li.label: the talks failed
li.description: I tried to make peace between those two families, and it ended in blood. I keep going over what I should have said.

li.label: the preacher's sermon
li.description: I went to hear the preacher on the road. I don't know if I believe a word of it, but I slept well afterward.

li.label: won the argument
li.description: I argued with the wandering preacher until the lamps burned low, and the preacher gave in first.

li.label: lost the argument
li.description: The preacher had an answer for everything I said. People have been looking at me differently since.

li.label: kept from following
li.description: I wanted to go with the preacher, and the council sent the preacher away instead. They didn't ask me what I thought.

li.label: arguments at supper
li.description: Every supper turns into an argument about the preacher's words. I just want to eat.

li.label: talked it out
li.description: We sat up most of the night and talked it all out, the preacher's words and everything else. We're eating at the same table again.

li.label: the rescue came back
li.description: We paid for a rescue for strangers, and it came back with people who would have died in that ruin.

li.label: pilgrims at our shrine
li.description: Pilgrims walked all the way from their town and stopped to pray at the sculpture we put up. I didn't think anyone would care that much about it.
